text: Resistance exercise elicits a combination of neural and muscular responses and adaptations. Although an increased protein synthetic response is seen after a single bout of resistance training, changes in muscle size are not observed for several weeks of consistent exercise (207). Moreover, appreciable muscle protein accumulation (commonly referred to as accretion ) generally takes a couple of months to become appreciably apparent (141). Early-phase increases in strength therefore are primarily attributed to neural improvements (141, 173, 196). Such observations follow the principles of motor learning.
